programs.name: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP)
programs.description: Federal food assistance program providing monthly benefits for groceries.
programs.what_it_does: Provides monthly EBT card benefits to purchase food at authorized retailers.
programs.who_qualifies: Households at or below 130% of the Federal Poverty Level with limited assets.
how_to_apply: Apply online at your state SNAP portal
Apply in person at local DSHS/DHS office
documents_needed: Social Security numbers for household members

programs.name: Medicaid
programs.description: Federal-state health insurance program for low-income individuals and families.
programs.what_it_does: Provides comprehensive health coverage including doctor visits, hospital stays, prescriptions, and mental health services.
programs.who_qualifies: Adults under 138% FPL in expansion states; children, pregnant women, elderly, and disabled individuals at varying thresholds.
how_to_apply: Apply at your state Medicaid office
documents_needed: Proof of citizenship or immigration status

programs.name: Housing Choice Voucher Program (Section 8)
programs.description: Federal rental assistance program that subsidizes housing costs for low-income families.
programs.what_it_does: Pays a portion of rent directly to landlords, with tenants paying roughly 30% of income toward rent.
programs.who_qualifies: Households at or below 50% of Area Median Income (AMI). Priority for extremely low income (30% AMI).
how_to_apply: Contact your local Public Housing Authority (PHA)
programs.deadlines: Waitlists open periodically — check with local PHA

programs.name: Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP)
programs.description: Federal program helping low-income households with energy costs.
programs.what_it_does: Provides assistance paying heating and cooling bills, energy crisis intervention, and weatherization.
programs.who_qualifies: Households at or below 150% FPL or 60% of state median income.
how_to_apply: Apply through local Community Action Agency
programs.agency: HHS Administration for Children and Families

programs.name: Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF)
programs.description: Federal-state cash assistance program for families with children.
programs.what_it_does: Provides monthly cash benefits, job training, childcare assistance, and other support services.
programs.who_qualifies: Very low-income families with dependent children. Income limits and time limits vary by state.
how_to_apply: Apply at your local DSHS/DHS office
programs.max_benefit: Varies by state ($200-$700/month depending on family size and state)
programs.agency: HHS Administration for Children and Families

programs.name: 2-1-1 Community Navigation
programs.description: Free, confidential referral service connecting people to local resources.
programs.what_it_does: Trained specialists help identify and connect callers to local services including food, housing, utilities, healthcare, and crisis support.

programs.name: National Domestic Violence Hotline
programs.description: 24/7 confidential support for domestic violence survivors.
programs.what_it_does: Provides crisis intervention, safety planning, and referrals to local DV shelters and legal services.
programs.who_qualifies: Anyone experiencing domestic violence, dating violence, or stalking.

programs.name: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
programs.description: 24/7 free crisis support for anyone in emotional distress or suicidal crisis.
programs.what_it_does: Connects callers to trained crisis counselors for immediate support, de-escalation, and referrals.
programs.who_qualifies: Anyone experiencing a mental health crisis, suicidal thoughts, or emotional distress.
